subject: Seeking help from Statistical Consultant for Cross-Regional Measurement Invariance

messages.author: 7523381519b35f0c
messages.subject: Seeking help from Statistical Consultant for Cross-Regional Measurement Invariance
parts:
Dear all,

I am very new to measurement invariance, and unfamiliar with some procedures, and would like to seek help from a statistical consultant who is familiar with MI. I would like to ask if there is/are statistical consultants who are willing to help, and/or if there are recommendations for statistical consultants so that I can contact.

I am conducting measurement invariance tests for a cross-regional study (Hong Kong China plus United Kingdom). While I know how to run basic MI (configural, metric, scalar) tests with lavaan, I am confused and I am not sure how to deal with situations that metric and/or scalar invariance is not supported - e.g. 1) how to interpret results and perhaps remove items based on DIF/modification index, 2) whether it is acceptable to run moderated regressions with the combined sample (Hong Kong China plus UK) or need to incorporate group-mean-centering (I asked Poe, not sure about this) or separate the samples, if there is evidence for metric invariance but not scalar invariance, etc. Will really appreciate if there is a statistical consultant who can guide me through these procedures step by step. Thank you!

Regards,
Kit
